evidenceAudit.scope: Primary health centre, screening centre and maternity unit staff in Saudi Arabia: explain and arrange premarital screening and genetic counselling for couples (sickle cell, thalassaemia, hepatitis B, hepatitis C, HIV), act on results, and make sure every newborn has the dried blood spot test at 24 to 72 hours with recall and treatment of positive results. Uses the Saudi Ministry of Health premarital page, Saudi programme data and the product labels. Not for prenatal diagnosis or the treatment of individual metabolic diseases.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-20.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: The Saudi Ministry of Health premarital page names the diseases screened (sickle cell anaemia, thalassaemia, hepatitis B, hepatitis C, HIV/AIDS), the three-month advance advice and the six-month validity of the certificate, but does not say what happens after a positive result; the counselling process described in the peer-reviewed study (mandatory screening and counselling since 2004) was not confirmed from an official protocol.
The page does not say whether screening is mandatory; the study describes a mandatory programme, so the topic reports both statements and does not assert a legal requirement.

The Ministry's official list of newborn screening conditions was not opened; the 23-disorder panel comes from a 2026 review of the programme's laboratory practice and may differ from the current Ministry list.

Details of how recall, treatment initiation and hearing or heart (critical congenital heart disease) screening are done in each region were not found; only the 24 to 48 hour recall target from the review is used.
Premarital counselling of couples who are both carriers is described as a risk discussion only; no Saudi protocol about pre-implantation or prenatal diagnosis was read, so none is written.

Levothyroxine for congenital hypothyroidism is written from the United States tablet label (10 to 15 mcg per kg per day for 0 to 3 months); the Saudi paediatric endocrine protocol and the target thyroid hormone values were not found and the treatment is for a paediatric endocrinologist to confirm and supervise.
Hepatitis B vaccination of a susceptible partner follows the US label's adult schedule (1 mL at 0, 1 and 6 months); Saudi vaccination guidance for adults was not checked.
Care of sickle cell disease and thalassaemia after a positive newborn screen (penicillin prophylaxis, folic acid, transfusion) was not reviewed, so no regimen is written for it.
Figures were read by automated extraction of web, article and label text; spot-check each figure and dose against the source during clinical review.

pathophysiology.summary: Sickle cell trait occurs in 4% to 7% of Saudis and beta-thalassaemia trait in 1.8% to 3.2%; about 56% of marriages are consanguineous, which raises the chance of affected children (Premarital screening beta-haemoglobin study, Section Introduction). In 1,871,184 people screened in 2011 to 2018, haemoglobin S was found in 4.7% and beta-thalassaemia in 1.2% (Premarital screening beta-haemoglobin study, Section Results). Inborn errors of metabolism are 4 to 5 times more frequent than in Western populations, driven by consanguinity (Saudi newborn screening review, Section 3.2). Newborn screening uses a dried blood spot taken 24 to 72 hours after birth and tested mainly by tandem mass spectrometry (Saudi newborn screening review, Section 3.3.1). Screening is not diagnosis: a positive screen is confirmed by plasma, urine or enzyme testing and, often, molecular testing (Saudi newborn screening review, Section 3.3.2).

symptoms: Couples have no symptoms: premarital screening finds carriers and infections before marriage (Saudi MOH Premarital Screening page, Section Overview).

A newborn with a positive screen may look well; treatment should start within the first 1 to 2 weeks of life because delays can cause irreversible damage (Saudi newborn screening review, Section 3.4).
A family history of sickle cell disease, thalassaemia or an inherited metabolic disease increases the importance of counselling (Premarital screening beta-haemoglobin study, Section Introduction).
physicalSigns: Carriers usually have no signs on examination; results come from blood tests (Premarital screening beta-haemoglobin study, Section Methods).
A newborn with a positive screen may have jaundice, poor feeding, lethargy, hypotonia, or vomiting (Saudi newborn screening review, Section 3.4).
redFlags: Newborn with a critical screening value or who is unwell with poor feeding, vomiting, lethargy or seizures: see within 24 to 48 hours and send urgently to a specialist centre (Saudi newborn screening review, Section 3.3.2).
Dried blood spot not collected by 72 hours, or specimen rejected: re-collect without delay (Saudi newborn screening review, Section 3.3.1).
Couple who are both carriers of the same haemoglobin variant: give genetic counselling before the marriage decision is finalised (Premarital screening beta-haemoglobin study, Section Discussion).
Positive hepatitis B, hepatitis C or HIV result: confirm, counsel privately, refer, and arrange care for the partner (Saudi MOH Premarital Screening page, Section Overview).
precipitants: Consanguineous marriage (about 56% of marriages) (Premarital screening beta-haemoglobin study, Section Introduction).
Residence in the Eastern and South-Western regions, where carrier rates are higher (Premarital screening beta-haemoglobin study, Section Introduction).
Family history of inherited blood or metabolic disease (Saudi newborn screening review, Section 3.2).
Birth outside a hospital in the screening network, which risks missed screening (Saudi newborn screening review, Section 1).

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Healthy person with one abnormal haemoglobin gene; risk arises in children of two carriers (Premarital screening beta-haemoglobin study, Section Results).
Symptomatic anaemia or sickle crises; confirmed by electrophoresis (Premarital screening beta-haemoglobin study, Section Methods).
Presumptive positive that is not confirmed by diagnostic testing (Saudi newborn screening review, Section 3.3.7).
Result normalises on repeat testing, for example transient thyroid-stimulating hormone rise (Saudi newborn screening review, Section 3.3.7).
Persistent abnormal metabolites confirmed by plasma, urine or enzyme testing (Saudi newborn screening review, Section 3.3.2).

clinicalManagement.title: Advise couples early
clinicalManagement.timeframe: At least three months before the wedding
actions: Tell couples planning marriage to book premarital screening, individually or together, at one of more than 300 centres, including via the booking service (Saudi MOH Premarital Screening page, Section Overview).
Explain the certificate is valid for six months (Saudi MOH Premarital Screening page, Section Overview).
If one partner lives outside the Kingdom, follow the page's steps for authentication and electronic submission of results (Saudi MOH Premarital Screening page, Section Overview).

clinicalManagement.title: Test the couple
actions: Take blood for haemoglobin electrophoresis or chromatography and for hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HIV tests (Premarital screening beta-haemoglobin study, Section Methods; Saudi MOH Premarital Screening page, Section Overview).
Repeat infectious disease tests when needed (Saudi MOH Premarital Screening page, Section Overview).

clinicalManagement.title: Give results and counselling
actions: Explain the meaning of carrier and disease states in each partner and the chance of an affected child, using the medical consultation offered by the programme (Saudi MOH Premarital Screening page, Section Overview).
Refer couples where both carry the same variant to the genetic counselling clinic (Premarital screening beta-haemoglobin study, Section Introduction).

Arrange care and private counselling for a positive hepatitis B, hepatitis C or HIV result, and offer hepatitis B vaccination to a susceptible partner (Engerix-B label, Section Dosage and Administration).

clinicalManagement.title: Collect the newborn blood spot
actions: Collect the dried blood spot at the birth hospital 24 to 72 hours after birth, air dry it at ambient temperature away from heat and sunlight, and send by the medical courier (Saudi newborn screening review, Section 3.3.1).
Record the infant's details and the family's contact numbers for recall (Saudi newborn screening review, Section 3.3.1).

clinicalManagement.title: Act on a positive result
actions: When the laboratory reports a critical value the regional coordinator arranges review within 24 to 48 hours (Saudi newborn screening review, Section 3.3.1).

Send diagnostic confirmation tests (plasma amino acids, urine organic acids, serum thyroid tests, enzyme or molecular testing) and refer to the specialist centre (Saudi newborn screening review, Section 3.3.2).

Start treatment as soon as the diagnosis is confirmed; for congenital hypothyroidism begin levothyroxine under a paediatric endocrinologist (Levothyroxine label, Section Dosage and Administration 2.4).

clinicalManagement.title: Close the loop
clinicalManagement.timeframe: First 1 to 2 weeks of life and ongoing
actions: Time to result and time to treatment should ideally fall within the first 1 to 2 weeks of life (Saudi newborn screening review, Section 3.4).
Record outcome of each recall and report missed screens to the programme (Saudi newborn screening review, Section 3.4).

regimens.indication: Active immunisation against hepatitis B in a susceptible adult partner of an infected person
regimens.dose: 1 mL (20 mcg) per dose, three doses on a 0-, 1- and 6-month schedule (Engerix-B label, Dosage and Administration 2.3). Dilution and preparation: none; shake well before use until a homogeneous turbid white suspension forms, and do not use if it looks otherwise or has particles or discolouration (Engerix-B label, Dosage and Administration 2.1).
regimens.route: Intramuscular injection into the deltoid; not into the buttock; subcutaneous injection is possible in people at risk of bleeding but gives a lower antibody response (Engerix-B label, Dosage and Administration 2.1 and 2.2)
adjustments: Adults on haemodialysis need four doses of 2 mL on a 0, 1, 2 and 6-month schedule (Engerix-B label, Dosage and Administration 2.3).
Fainting can occur after any injected vaccine; have a procedure to prevent injury (Engerix-B label, Warnings 5.1).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Observe for fainting and allergic reaction after the injection (Engerix-B label, Warnings 5.1).
Antibody response in those at risk of poor response, per local policy (Engerix-B label, Dosage and Administration 2.3).
contraindications: Severe allergic reaction (for example anaphylaxis) after a previous dose of any hepatitis B vaccine or to any component, including yeast (Engerix-B label, Contraindications 4).

regimens.indication: Congenital hypothyroidism confirmed after a positive newborn screen
regimens.patientGroup: Newborn infants aged 0 to 3 months with confirmed congenital hypothyroidism
regimens.dose: 10 to 15 mcg per kg per day for age 0 to 3 months; start at the full daily dose in most infants, and consider a lower starting dose in newborns at risk of cardiac failure, increasing every 4 to 6 weeks as needed (Levothyroxine label, Dosage and Administration 2.4). Dilution and preparation: for an infant who cannot swallow a tablet, crush the tablet, suspend it in 5 to 10 mL (1 to 2 teaspoons) of water and give at once by spoon or dropper; do not store the suspension; do not mix with soybean-based infant formula (Levothyroxine label, Dosage and Administration 2.1).
regimens.route: Oral, as a single daily dose on an empty stomach one-half to one hour before feeding where possible; give at least 4 hours apart from drugs that reduce absorption (Levothyroxine label, Dosage and Administration 2.1)
regimens.duration: Long-term; adjusted to clinical response and thyroid tests under paediatric endocrine care (Levothyroxine label, Dosage and Administration 2.4)
adjustments: Doses for older children fall with age: 8 to 10 mcg per kg for 3 to 6 months, 6 to 8 for 6 to 12 months, 5 to 6 for 1 to 5 years (Levothyroxine label, Dosage and Administration 2.4, Table 1).
Soybean-based formula, iron, calcium and some other products reduce absorption (Levothyroxine label, Drug Interactions 7).
Uncorrected adrenal insufficiency must be treated first (Levothyroxine label, Contraindications 4).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Clinical response, growth and heart rate (Levothyroxine label, Dosage and Administration 2.4).
Serum thyroid stimulating hormone and free thyroxine, with free thyroxine in the upper half of the normal range (Levothyroxine label, Dosage and Administration 2.3 and 2.4).
Signs of over-treatment: fast heart rate, irritability, poor sleep, diarrhoea (Levothyroxine label, Warnings 5.1).

medicationPlan.note: The screening itself uses no medicine. Two follow-up medicines are written because they are the direct consequence of a screening result: hepatitis B vaccine for a susceptible partner, and levothyroxine for a newborn with confirmed congenital hypothyroidism. Doses, dilution, administration and contraindications come from the product labels named in each row. SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.

learningObjectives: Advise couples to be screened at least three months before the wedding.
Collect the newborn blood spot at 24 to 72 hours and protect specimen quality.
A positive newborn screen needs confirmatory tests and review within 24 to 48 hours.
Start levothyroxine promptly for confirmed congenital hypothyroidism.
pitfalls: Late collection of the blood spot.
Telling the family that a positive screen is a diagnosis.
Missing hepatitis B vaccination for the partner.
keyPoints: The premarital certificate lasts six months.
Both partners carrying the same variant need counselling.
Start treatment only after the diagnosis is confirmed, except for the urgent steps the specialist directs.

patientEducation: Premarital screening tells you whether you or your partner carry blood conditions such as sickle cell or thalassaemia, or infections such as hepatitis.
Book at least three months before your wedding; the certificate is valid for six months.
Being a carrier usually does not make you ill but it can affect your children.
Every baby has a heel-prick blood spot test in the first days of life.
If the test is positive, it does not mean your baby has the disease; more tests are needed quickly.
Keep your phone number up to date so we can reach you.
lifestyleAndDiet: Attend genetic counselling together if both partners are carriers.
Complete the hepatitis B vaccine course if advised.
Bring the newborn screening card to the child's first clinic visit.
Share the result with your family doctor.
mdtReferrals: Primary health centre doctor and nurse; genetic counsellor; haematologist; midwife and neonatal nurse; newborn screening coordinator; paediatric endocrinologist and metabolic specialist; laboratory team.
dischargeCriteria: Premarital result and counselling documented; certificate issued; newborn blood spot collected with correct details; recall contact confirmed; follow-up for positive results scheduled.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Couples: repeat tests only if advised; vaccinate susceptible partners at 0, 1 and 6 months. Newborns: confirmatory review within 24 to 48 hours of a critical result; treatment follow-up under the specialist team.
